outcome: Maternal admission to intensive care unit (ICU)
cohort: 27,807 women who delivered at Sant'Anna Hospital, Turin, between 2011 and 2015
finding: A 10% decrease in pre-pregnancy BMI was associated with a reduction of at least 15% in several adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes, including GDM, preeclampsia, maternal ICU admission, macrosomia, low APGAR scores, and neonatal ICU admission.
mod_finding: Larger differences in BMI (20-25%) corresponded to at least a 10% reduction in the risk of preterm and very preterm delivery and emergency cesarean section.
